decision: let each layer, including pstack, name its source as owner/repo@ref, a git URL, or a local path, with per-run overrides recorded in the lock and reported by status and update

evidence: docs/master-template.md; scripts/Install-Workspace.ps1 LayerSource handling
result: design recorded in phase 0; nothing built

decision: record an owned list in stack.lock.json for every path -Apply writes, and add -Status, which compares the list with the disk and with the plan, writes nothing, and exits 1 with -Strict when a path is not matching
why: remove and uninstall may delete only what the installer wrote, so the lock needs a hash, target, or entry per path, and status can report drift without writing; Pi lists are recorded per entry so user keys stay out of the record
evidence: scripts/Install-Workspace.test.mjs and scripts/verify-manifests.test.mjs: 12 installer cases and 6 manifest cases fail on upstream/main's installer and verifiers; the real D:\dev\simpsonm09 status reports no ownership record and exits 0, or 1 with -Strict
result: branch feat/ownership-record; the owner must review the design choices in the PR report before merge, and the real workspace needs one -Apply to write its record

decision: fix the review findings on the ownership record: an owned folder is wholly the installer's (apply removes extras and prints each one); a tree hash does not follow links and sorts by UTF-8 bytes in PowerShell and Python; the claude treeSha256 keeps the legacy rule; the record names createdDirs, createdFiles, createdKey, and the .bak backups; a Pi entry the user already lists is not recorded
why: a record must hold what the installer wrote and nothing else, so a user file in an owned folder is removed, not adopted; the legacy rule keeps existing claude values valid; a path that the installer did not create is never listed as created
evidence: installer suite 77 tests, 75 pass and 2 skipped; 15 of the new installer tests and 2 manifest tests fail on the branch head; the temp apply and -Status report 18 of 18 matching with createdDirs and opencode.jsonc.bak recorded
result: owner review: the legacy rule matches node_modules without regard to case, as PowerShell -ne did, while the owned rule is exact; uninstall and remove are not built yet

decision: add -Runtimes and -Layers to the installer: the selection is recorded in stack.lock.json, flags add to it and never narrow it, copilot and pi need claude, a local claude layer without opencode is a copy of its items, and an unselected runtime's files are left alone and status names them not selected
why: a workspace must install a subset of runtimes without writing or judging the rest, and the lock must record what was installed so update, status, and remove can reuse it; narrowing is the remove command, which is a later step
evidence: node --test scripts/*.test.mjs: 126 tests, 124 pass, 2 skipped (main had 111, 109 pass); the 15 new selection tests fail on upstream/main's installer (75 pass, 15 fail); just check, lint-full, complexity, validate, aislop (score 97), security and check-standard pass; verify-manifests passes; verify-workspace-install on the real workspace fails only on the missing ownership record, as on main
result: branch feat/selection; the owner decides before merge whether copilot needs claude, the layer default of a fresh lock, and the copy-of-items case for a local claude layer

decision: review fixes: a recorded layer or runtime that layers.json no longer names is dropped with a warning instead of failing; a layer or runtime that layers.json names but the selection leaves out is named on apply, audit, and status with the flag that adds it; stack.lock.json is replaced whole through a temporary file and the replaced lock is kept as .bak; an empty, null, or truncated lock is refused with recovery steps and the cost of deleting it; the verifiers refuse an enabled pi or copilot block for an unselected runtime
why: a removed layer made every command fail, a layer added to layers.json was silently never installed by a plain apply, a truncated or empty lock failed with a PowerShell error, and an enabled block for an unselected runtime passed the verifiers
evidence: node --test scripts/*.test.mjs: 136 tests, 134 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped (POSIX-only, as before); 9 of the 16 new or changed selection tests fail on e3a23e4, and the other 7 are regression guards that pass on it; no Python-dependent test skips here; just check, lint-full, complexity, validate, security, aislop (score 97), check-standard, and verify-manifests pass
result: branch feat/selection, local commit only; the owner still decides the copilot-needs-claude rule and the other points in the earlier report

decision: add -Remove and -Uninstall: a dry run by default that prints DELETE, RESTORE, KEEP, or SKIP for each path, and -Apply executes; each record is deleted only while the disk still matches it, a junction is removed as a link, a replaced file is put back from its backup only while it holds the installer text, and a skip keeps its record in the lock so a retry finishes
why: a removal must never delete a user file, so the record names each path runtime and layer, the delete checks are the only route to a delete, and an interrupted run leaves a lock that a retry finishes; the round trip returns the user config and Pi settings byte for byte
evidence: node --test scripts/*.test.mjs: 154 tests, 152 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped (POSIX only); 16 new removal tests and 2 changed installer tests fail on upstream/main, and 2 new and 5 changed verifier tests fail on main verify_ownership; just check, lint-full, complexity, validate, aislop (score 97, one pre-existing file-size warning), security, check-standard, and both verify scripts pass; the real workspace is read only by -Status and the verifiers, and no -Remove or -Uninstall ran against it
result: branch feat/remove-uninstall, local commits only, not pushed; the owner decides whether a hand edit may replace the first backup, whether a missing owned file should finish an uninstall, and the Co-Authored-By line

decision: record the consistency of AI behavior across the seven runtimes as a parity matrix with evidence per cell, and let the neutral skill source carry non-portable frontmatter keys that the generator strips per runtime
why: the plan promises consistent behavior or a documented reason, and 24 of 58 PStack skills already use a key outside the portable subset
evidence: docs/parity-matrix.md; frontmatter check of the 58 PStack skills; live Pi checks of 2026-10-09

decision: an npm-written package-lock.json beside a layer package.json is removed after npm unless the layer ships one, and a shipped lock is put back as shipped; the ownership record covers exactly what the installer wrote; the same applies to npm-shrinkwrap.json, and a shipped read-only lock is rewritten only when its bytes differ
why: the lock check treated a directory item named opencode as copying opencode/package-lock.json, so npm lock stayed in the pstack folder and the folder no longer matched its plan, failing the apply at Assert-Written
evidence: real npm install in a temporary workspace reproduces the Assert-Written error at .opencode/plugins/pstack; the only path that differs from the plan is opencode/package-lock.json; forcing the removal makes the apply pass; four of the five new npm regression tests fail on main, and the extra-file guard passes there as intended
result: fixed on fix/assert-written-npm; gates run before each commit

decision: implement -Source and -LayerSource layer overrides, the source block in stack.lock.json, the layer-source block in -Status and audit, and -Update with -Check, as the layer-sources section of master-template.md specifies
why: a fork branch or a local checkout of PStack could not be tried without editing layers.json, nothing reported an override or a branch that moves, and update was not built
evidence: 23 of the new or changed installer and verifier tests fail on upstream/main; the shape guard that accepts valid source blocks passes there by design; node suite 217 tests, 215 pass, 2 skipped; just check, lint-full, complexity, aislop, security, and check-standard pass
result: implemented on Windows; the lock's source string becomes an object with legacy strings still accepted, a local override records an absolute path, and macOS is not started

decision: npm keeps --ignore-scripts with no opt-out, and an apply that runs npm names each layer whose install scripts or binding.gyp did not run
why: a layer's install scripts and its native build run code from a checkout the installer reads, so the flag stays; without a warning, a layer that declares one installs without it and the run says nothing
evidence: tests: an apply that runs npm names a layer that declares an install script, one that ships a binding.gyp, and a layer with neither prints no ignore-scripts warning

decision: the installer requires PowerShell 7 (#requires -Version 7.0), and Windows PowerShell 5.1 is not supported, with no compatibility layer
why: the script uses PowerShell 7 APIs that 5.1 cannot parse, so under powershell.exe it stopped with a parse error and no requirement; a version check at the top gives one clear reason, and a 5.1 port would be a second code path to keep
evidence: test: the installer under powershell.exe exits non-zero with the requirement and no parse error; the OpenCode verifier parses under 5.1 and uses no PowerShell 7 syntax, so it carries no requirement

decision: the filter guard passes its settings in the git child's environment, reads only the tree's own config (local and worktree, with includes), refuses a name it cannot pass or more than 100 names, and reads no tree attributes on a local status
why: -c arguments split a filter name at its first equals sign, so its filter ran; reading every config scope turned off the user's git-lfs filter, so checkouts installed pointer files
evidence: tests: a name with an equals sign does not run its filter; a control-character name makes the tree unreadable; 101 names are refused and 100 read; a global smudge still runs in a guarded checkout; a global filter named only by in-tree attributes does not run on status
